standard_prerequisites: Same chapter: lemma-normal-closure-inside-normal (finite Galois E containing any finite K(S) inside L), lemma-finite-finitely-generated (finite extensions are finitely generated), lemma-ses-galois (restriction maps G_lambda -> G_lambda' surjective in towers of finite Galois extensions), lemma-galois-infinite (canonical surjective continuous restriction Gal(L/K) -> Gal(L_lambda/K))

Categories, Definition categories-definition-directed-system and Section categories-section-directed-colimits: directed posets and the description of filtered colimits of fields as unions; Topology, Lemma topology-lemma-topological-group-limits (limits of topological groups commute with the forgetful functor) and topology-lemma-bijective-map (a bijective continuous map of profinite spaces is a homeomorphism); cited as standard facts of sibling chapters
core_obligations: Lambda (finite Galois subextensions L_lambda/K, ordered by inclusion) is directed: two of them are contained in a third by taking the normal closure of the union of generators
L = colim L_lambda as K-extensions, since every element of L lands in some L_lambda and filtered colimits of fields are unions
G_lambda forms an inverse system of finite groups with surjective transition maps (restriction, by lemma-ses-galois), and the restriction maps assemble a continuous bijection G -> lim G_lambda
The bijection is a homeomorphism because both sides are profinite (Topology, topology-lemma-bijective-map), and each projection G -> G_lambda is continuous and surjective
proof_roadmap: Prove Lambda nonempty and directed and identify the colimit of the L_lambda with L
Assemble the inverse system of the G_lambda with surjective transitions
Build the canonical continuous bijection G -> lim G_lambda and upgrade it to a homeomorphism
